system.longDesc: Sometimes called demolition mechs, salvage mechs are one of the most common mechs in use at spaceports and other places where spacecraft operate. These mechs excel at both making repairs and slicing up large masses, usually asteroids, ice masses, and parts of ships. Salvage mechs are bright yellow with a vacuum-sealed, egg-shaped cage for the driver and have four legs. Each leg ends with a three-fingered manipulator claw; the rear legs can magnetically adhere to a structure while the front two use a variety of cutting and welding tools. Salvage mechs can operate under their own thrust in space and have enough propellant and oxygen to allow a driver to work for several hours. Additional tools include x-ray scanners, a sealant foam injector the operator can use to keep from venting air when working on a sealed craft or habitat, and fire suppression gear.
